description: Our team aims to develop a platform that uses live satellite tracking data to identify, monitor, and visualize satellites passing over a specific geographical area. The project will help users discover which satellites are overhead, how many pass through an area, and their movement patterns. By making real-time satellite data accessible through an interactive map, we hope to make space technology more understandable, engaging, and useful.
summary:
FIELD//WATCH: Agricultural Satellite & Soil Decision-Support System

What We Developed:

FIELD//WATCH is a browser-based agricultural decision-support tool that provides real-time field monitoring for any coordinate on Earth. It integrates NASA/USGS Landsat and ESA Sentinel-2 Earth observations, a 7-day satellite orbit pass tracker, an interactive 3D terrain visualizer, and a 16-day microclimate deck tracking multi-depth soil moisture, soil temperature, reference evapotranspiration, and vapor pressure deficit.

How It Addresses the Challenge:

FIELD//WATCH transforms orbital imagery and local soil physics into practical crop rotation and soil protection strategies. Its hybrid agronomic engine—combining an offline deterministic rule system with a private, client-side AI agronomist—evaluates moisture deficits, thermal accumulation, and disease risks to help growers plan sustainable rotations, conserve topsoil moisture, and schedule operations.

Why It Is Important:

Climate shifts, irregular rainfall, and soil degradation make crop rotation decisions increasingly volatile. FIELD//WATCH democratizes NASA-grade Earth observations and root-zone soil telemetry without paywalls, subscriptions, or backend data harvesting, empowering growers worldwide to build soil vitality and long-term farm resilience.
details:
PROJECT DETAILS

1. What Does It Do and How Does It Work?

FIELD//WATCH operates as a zero-installation, privacy-first web application accessible on desktop, tablet, and mobile devices:

  • Location Search & GIS Mapping: Farmers search by local place name or input precise GPS coordinates. The application centers on the target farm and establishes a focused 0.03° bounding box (approximately 6.6 km × 6.6 km).
    • Deterministic Local Rule Engine: Runs completely offline, evaluating 12+ agronomic thresholds such as root-zone irrigation deficits, soil drying risks, frost hazards, heat stress, mildew leaf-wetness incubation, and low-drift spray windows.
    • BYOK AI Agronomist: Allows farmers to optionally enter their own AI API key (OpenAI or compatible endpoints). The AI reads the farm's telemetry locally and drafts an operational advisory brief.

2. What Benefits Does It Have?

  • Bridging Orbit and Root-Zone: Connects macro-scale satellite flyovers with micro-scale root-zone soil physics on a single screen.
  • 100% Client-Side Privacy: Operates entirely inside the farmer's web browser. Farm coordinates, field notes, and API keys are never stored on an external server or sold to third parties.
  • Immediate Operational Guidance: Converts abstract atmospheric and spectral numbers into concrete daily farm actions (e.g., specific low-drift spraying time slots, irrigation shortfall in millimeters, and topsoil preservation alerts).
  • Zero Overhead and High Availability: Requires no account creation, proprietary hardware, or expensive subscriptions.

3. What Is the Intended Impact?

  • Optimized Crop Rotations: Gives farmers the temporal soil moisture and temperature context needed to time cover crops, balance nutrient-depleting crops with nitrogen-fixing varieties, and sustain multi-year rotation resilience.
  • Water & Soil Conservation: Tracking cumulative water balance (ET0\text{ET}_0ET0​ versus precipitation) prevents over-irrigation, protects ground aquifers, and stops unnecessary tillage when topsoil moisture is vulnerable to erosion.
  • Democratizing Earth Observations: Brings NASA and ESA satellite capabilities—traditionally limited to large industrial agribusinesses—directly to smallholder farmers and agricultural cooperatives globally.

4. Tools, Coding Languages, Hardware, and Software

  • Programming Languages: Vanilla JavaScript (ES6+), HTML5, CSS3, Scalable Vector Graphics (SVG).
    • Three.js & OrbitControls: Renders the 3D terrain mesh, atmospheric phenomena, and satellite skin.
    • satellite.js (v5.0.0): Performs high-precision orbital SGP4 satellite propagation client-side.
    • Leaflet.js (v1.9.4): Interactive 2D mapping and ground track vector overlays.
    • Hand-Coded SVG Charts: Zero-dependency, lightweight mathematical rendering of polar wind roses, time series, and atmospheric vertical soundings.
    • NASA / USGS Landsat 8 & 9 and ESA Sentinel-2 via Microsoft Planetary Computer STAC API.
    • CelesTrak NORAD Elements: Real-time satellite ephemeris data.
    • Open-Meteo APIs: Global weather, soil moisture, elevation, marine, and air quality models.
    • OpenStreetMap / Nominatim: Geocoding and reverse geocoding.
  • Hardware Requirements: Runs on standard laptops, tablets, or smartphones with any modern WebGL-capable browser.

5. How Is the Project Creative?

  • Live 3D Farm Digital Twin: Rather than relying on flat data tables, it builds an animated 3D topographic replica of the field where elevation relief, wind particle speeds, and cloud decks react in real time to actual local weather.
  • Neo-Brutalist Visual Design: Employs high-contrast typography, crisp visual cards, and clear status chips engineered for strong legibility on handheld devices under bright outdoor sunlight.
  • In-Browser Satellite Pass Computation: Instead of querying pre-compiled proprietary databases, the browser calculates satellite flybys and viewing angles in real time using celestial physics.
  • Zero-Bloat Custom Graphics: All meteograms and polar wind roses are drawn using mathematical vector paths, eliminating heavy third-party dashboard libraries and ensuring instant load times.

6. Factors Considered by the Team

  • Low-Bandwidth Rural Access: Optimized code to run without heavy frontend frameworks (React, Angular), utilizing local caching (such as 2-hour satellite ephemerides) to minimize cellular data consumption.
  • Farmer Data Sovereignty: Farm locations and operational parameters remain strictly on the user’s device; no backend server tracks user behavior.
  • Handling Cloud Cover: Because optical sensors cannot penetrate heavy cloud cover, the system automatically checks scene cloud percentages, notifies the grower when satellite pixels are obscured, and steers their attention toward ground-level soil sensors and weather trends.
  • Reliable Fallback Logic: Guaranteed offline utility through the built-in deterministic rule engine, ensuring growers receive sound agronomic advice even without an active AI key or external LLM service.
